heading: INT. BUS STATION WAITING ROOM - 2 A.M.

units.text: INT. BUS STATION WAITING ROOM - 2 A.M.
Rows of molded seats.
A flickering departures board.
A vending machine hums beside a rack of dead pamphlets.
A mop and bucket stand abandoned by the door.
GWENDOLYN ASARE-BLACK, forties, sits alone with a paper cup and a cardboard box on her lap.
Across the room, an old man, LAZARUS PRENTISS, seventies, sleeps sitting up, chin on his chest, a harmonica in his hand.
By the board, a girl of fifteen, JUNIPER WOLCOTT-BAI, kicks a pebble against the wall with her sneaker, over and over, and sometimes glances at the box.
Gwendolyn tilts the lid up an inch, looks inside, and closes it.
Juniper kicks the pebble.
It skips across the tile and stops at Gwendolyn's shoe.
Gwendolyn picks it up, turns it over, and rolls it back across the floor.
Juniper traps it with her toe.
Lazarus stirs, plays two soft notes on the harmonica, and falls back asleep with his mouth open.
The departures board clicks.
A new line appears: DELAYED.
Gwendolyn sets the box on the seat beside her and puts her hand flat on the lid.
What's in it?
units.name: JUNIPER

units.text: My mother.
units.name: GWENDOLYN

units.text: Oh.
units.name: JUNIPER

units.text: Juniper picks up the pebble and crosses the room.
She sits one seat from the box, then holds out the pebble.
Gwendolyn takes it and tucks it into her pocket without a word.
They sit.
The vending machine hums.
